B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The vendor does not state a separate MCP charge or plan requirement. The official MCP setup requires an active Unthread account; the docs separately mention a ChatGPT plan or workspace that supports MCP connectors.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The official pricing page lists Pro starting at $85 per agent/month, minimum 5 seats; Business and Enterprise pricing is not listed as a fixed amount. All plans include a 14-day free trial.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Official pricing page notes conversation limits apply. It displays Annual and Monthly billing options but the extracted page does not establish which option corresponds to the $85 starting price.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth sign-in to an Unthread account and authorization to a workspace are documented. The service-account alternative requires an API key header. Plan, role, allowlist, and rate-limit requirements for the input endpoint are not specified.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and workspace permissions; OAuth access is described as limited to data the user is permitted to view. Plan and admin controls are vendor/workspace-admin managed.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge referencing protected-resource metadata. Both protected-resource documents report resource https://app.unthread.io/api/mcp, authorization server https://app.unthread.io, scopes_supported ["mcp"], and bearer_methods_supported ["header"]. Authorization-server metadata reports issuer https://app.unthread.io; authorization_endpoint https://app.unthread.io/oauth/authorize; token_endpoint https://app.unthread.io/api/oauth/token; registration_endpoint https://app.unthread.io/api/oauth/register; client_id_metadata_document_supported true; response_types_supported ["code"]; grant_types_supported ["authorization_code","refresh_token"]; code_challenge_methods_supported ["S256"]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ["none"]; scopes_supported ["mcp"]. The docs say OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and revocable access. Token lifetime and revocation endpoint are not specified. OpenID configuration returned 404, stating OIDC discovery is not supported.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration endpoint advertised at https://app.unthread.io/api/oauth/register; OAuth authorization code and refresh token grants; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth method none; scopes_supported ["mcp"]; bearer via header. Protected-resource metadata advertises authorization_servers ["https://app.unthread.io"]. Endpoint challenge: Bearer resource_metadata="https://app.unthread.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp".

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs identify five read-only survey tools and three write tools. No tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview-confirm flow is documented; create_approval_request creates a product approval request but is not documented as a prerequisite for other writes. 3. OAuth metadata scopes are ["mcp"]; docs say access is limited to data the user may view and can be disconnected in Unthread settings. Role inheritance is implied by that statement; token lifetime, revocation endpoint, redirect approval, allowlists, and admin enablement are Unknown. 4. No input-endpoint read-only mode, tool filter, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional endpoint variant is documented. Separate portal and WebMCP surfaces exist. 5. Vendor security page describes encryption, RBAC, and regional data hosting; MCP-specific masking or field exclusions are not stated. 6. MCP rate limits, quotas, result caps, and per-call costs are Unknown. 7. Docs mention survey request wrappers with Zod list/field allowlists and state startDate/endDate must be provided together for survey analytics filtering. No broader validation or correction behavior is described. 8. MCP-specific audit logging and telemetry are Unknown. 9. No feedback, rating, survey-to-vendor, or upsell tool appears in the documented eight-tool list; the tools provide survey data operations. 10. No MCP-delivered skill is documented. Official docs provide user-facing example prompts, not enforceable server rules. 11. Cross-call memory or state affecting tools/results is Unknown. 12. The input endpoint is a hosted endpoint; portal MCP and WebMCP are other official surfaces with different access/setup. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or universal escape-hatch tool is documented.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Use get_survey_analytics date-range validation (requires startDate and endDate together) for date filtering.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Unthread documents distinct MCP surfaces: the global app endpoint, customer-specific portal endpoints, and dashboard WebMCP. They have separate setup and capability descriptions. The available evidence does not establish that these are subservers behind the input endpoint.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official Unthread MCP page names 8 tools (5 survey tools and 3 write tools) and states no separate total. actions.json includes those 8 official names first, plus 6 names listed by the third-party Claude connector directory (2026-10-27); Manufact independently lists the same 6. The Claude listing is publisher-verified. MartechDB reports 8 documented tools and names the same official eight, but its snapshot says read 2026-10-10. MCP.so has no list. Agent Discoverability reports 7 tools for a ChatGPT plugin/discovery surface with proxy-style wrappers; these are not treated as names for this endpoint.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs provide suggested prompts, including “List my open conversations” and “What’s our ticket volume trend this month?” These are examples for the user/client, not documented server-enforced instructions.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The MCP documentation says: “The AI assistant can only access data you have permission to view”; “You can disconnect the integration at any time from your Unthread settings”; and “your password is never shared with Claude.” The security page describes SOC 2 Type II, TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, RBAC, and regional dedicated databases. These are vendor statements, not independently verified here.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The docs describe OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and workspace authorization. The pricing page offers a 14-day trial for all plans.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth challenge and metadata support authorization. Scope-level permission inheritance and revocability are documented but not verifiable from public code. The access restriction and security claims are documentation promises; no public server implementation was available to compare. No MCP-specific audit, retention, or AI-training behavior was established.

contradictions: The official MCP docs name 8 tools, while the Claude connector directory and Manufact list 6 names. The six catalogue names are added as third-party entries after the official eight; tool schemas and overlap with official capabilities are not published in the official docs.

The official page says the MCP supports reading conversations, users, analytics, knowledge base, custom fields/ticket types, and surveys, but explicitly names only five survey read tools and three writes. The Claude directory lists read tool names for current user, conversations, analytics, and custom fields that the official page does not enumerate.

MartechDB reports eight tools and names the eight in the official documentation; its recorded tool snapshot date is 2026-10-10. This differs from the six names shown in the Claude directory and Manufact listing.
observations_for_research: The official docs publish names for only part of the described read surface and do not publish MCP input schemas or tool annotations.
OAuth protected-resource metadata publishes a single scope, "mcp", while the docs describe authorization as limited to the user's product permissions.
The vendor documents a separate API-domain service-account configuration, a per-portal MCP variant, and a browser-session WebMCP integration.
